$schema-note: Companion to the Strings*.resx catalogues in this directory, for issue #552.
Every catalogue already carries every KEY - HyperWhisper.Localization.Tests
asserts the base key count and CatalogValidator asserts the key sets match.
Neither looked at VALUES, so a catalogue could hold all 864 keys and still be
half raw English. 36 of the 39 were.
'identicalByDesign' lists the keys whose value is SUPPOSED to be the English
string in every language: product names, vendor names, model ids. Translating
one of these would be the regression, not the fix. Each entry carries its
reason so the list stays reviewable. Values containing no letters at all
('{0}', '127.0.0.1:{0}') need no entry - the validator exempts them by rule.
'ceilings' is the ratchet. For each locale it is the number of TRANSLATABLE
keys (base keys minus the by-design set minus the letterless ones) whose value
is still byte-identical to English. CatalogValidator fails the build when a
locale exceeds its ceiling, so the number can only go down. A newly added key
that is not translated pushes all 39 locales one over their ceiling at once,
which is the point: a new untranslated string cannot land silently.
After a translation batch, reseed with:
python3 .claude/skills/localisation-syncer/scripts/windows/untranslated_resx.py --seed
'sharedValueCeiling' is the gate for issue #574, the neighbouring defect:
values that are present, not English, and WRONG. The bulk cause is a base
value being rewritten while the 39 catalogues keep a translation of the old
English. No per-value check can see that, but the AGREEMENT can - twenty
independent translators do not produce the same string by accident. So a
(key, value) pair carried by more than this many locales, and not equal to
the English, fails the build. Seven keys were in that state when the number
was introduced, including one that told every non-English user the Grok
model was 'slower' and one that named macOS's Finder in the Windows app.
The largest honest coincidence in these catalogues is 'Mikrofon', shared by
13 languages, so 20 leaves real headroom. Retranslate, never raise it.
'foreignPlatformTerms' is the third #574 gate and the cheapest. These are
the WINDOWS catalogues, so a localised value naming macOS furniture that the
English does not is a defect: 'Show in Explorer' was 'Im Finder anzeigen' in
35 of them, and the on-device blurb said 'runs entirely on your Mac' in 34.
Matching is whole-word and case-insensitive; the declined forms are listed
because Czech had 'na tvém Macu'. The list is data so that a false positive
- a language where one of these is an ordinary word - is fixed by deleting a
line here, not by editing a validator that three heads build.
Audit the heuristic neighbours of that class - a locale value equal to the
English of a DIFFERENT key, and translations that diverge wildly in length
from a base value that was rewritten under them - with:
python3 .claude/skills/localisation-syncer/scripts/windows/untranslated_resx.py --audit
